{{short description|Polish neuroscientist}}
'''Magdalena Götz''' (born 17 January 1962) is a German
<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.synergy-munich.de/members/investigators/goetz/cv/index.html|title=Curriculum vitae Prof. Dr. Magdalena Götz - Munich Cluster for Systems Neurology - LMU Munich|website=www.synergy-munich.de|language=en|access-date=7 March 2019|archive-date=27 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227060255/https://www.synergy-munich.de/members/investigators/goetz/cv/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[neuroscientist]]. She is noted for her study of [[Neuroglia|glial cells]] and holds a chair at [[LMU Munich]]'s Department of [[Physiology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/service/press/press_releases/2006/press_release_no_66/index.html |title=Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize site |publisher=Dfg.de |date= |accessdate=4 February 2014}}</ref> She is involved in the field of adult [[neurogenesis]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Eva Amsen |date=15 August 2011 |title=Interview with Magdalena Götz at ''Development'' |url=http://dev.biologists.org/content/138/16/3341.full |journal=Development |publisher=Dev.biologists.org |volume=138 |issue=16 |pages=3341–3342 |doi=10.1242/dev.066027 |pmid=21791525 |doi-access=free |accessdate=4 February 2014|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Götz discovered that [[Glial Cells|glial cells]] are [[neural stem cell]]s in the developing mammalian [[brain]].<ref name=":1" /> Current investigations study the mechanisms involved in determining how adult neural stem cells are [[Cellular differentiation|specified]]. Götz current work focuses on refining ways to reprogram glial cells into neurons in organisms with [[traumatic brain injury]].  [https://gscn.org/ The German Stem Cell Network] published an [https://www.eurostemcell.org/gscn-video-magdalena-gotz-neuronal-stem-cells interview] with Götz in 2015 explaining her research field.

== Early life and education ==
Götz studied [[Biology]] between the years 1982 and 1989 at the [[University of Tübingen]], [[Germany]] and in [[Zürich]], [[Switzerland]].<ref name=":0" /> She was promoted in 1992 to the position of [[Dr. rer. nat.]] at the [[Friedrich Miescher Laboratory of the Max Planck Society|Friedrich-Miescher Laboratory]] of the [[Max Planck Society|Max-Planck Society]], [[Tübingen]]. After her promotion and until 1996, she was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[National Institute for Medical Research]], [[London]] and Smith Kline Beecham, Harlow.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Götz led an independent Research Group at the [[Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology|Max-Planck Institute of Neurobiology]] in [[Martinsried]], [[Munich]] between 1997 and 2003. She has been the Director of the Institute of Stem Cell Research at the [https://www.helmholtz-munich.de/en/helmholtz-zentrum-muenchen/index.html Helmholtz Center Munich] since 2004. Götz has been chair of Physiological Genomics at [[LMU Munich]]. Since 2011, Götz has held a Research Professorship at LMU.

Götz is a member of the Synergy Board as well as a [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]] in the [https://www.synergy-munich.de/index.html Münch Cluster for Systems Neurology], also known as Synergy.
